gate.reason: An idea, not a defect (the raw note's own framing): no consumer exists. `EdgeTargetFacts` (sdk/src/kind.ts:841) declares the closed set as exactly five engine-derived facts and its doc says 'no convenience additions beyond'; no `handle` fact appears anywhere in `src/` or `sdk/src/`. Revive when a render hook wants a spelling those five (name, address, kind, host-relative path, repo-rooted path) cannot already express cleanly — the demand has to come from a hook author, not from the surface's own symmetry.

edit.description: Anticipated: a `handle` fact on the kind declaration, surfaced to a render hook as a sixth member of `EdgeTargetFacts` (841) beside the five it closes over today. It is the one fact of the six read off the *target kind's* declaration rather than derived from the resolved target member, so admitting it widens what 'derived at emit, never authored at the instance' means — the argument the consumer must carry.

summary: A kind-declared citable handle ('how a reference to a member of this kind reads') — a lower-priority idea, not a defect, with no consumer yet.
acceptance: A kind declaring `handle` lets a reference render hook spell a member of that kind without hand-rolling the branch on target.kind — provable once a real render hook wants one.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade, idea). Gate re-tested this audit and rewritten: the closed set is five on disk, so a handle would be the sixth fact, not the fifth the prior spelling claimed.
